plan.title: Freshness contract: bound vs live generation for long-lived multi-agent sessions after deposit upgrade

narratives.Description: After CLI or deposit upgrade, long-lived multi-agent sessions may still execute pre-upgrade payload while disk probes report up to date. This story ships a host-agnostic freshness contract: monotonic generation on apply, session bind of that generation, and a freshness report comparing bound vs live with current|stale_soft|stale_hard states plus rebind guidance that does not require restarting the shared host runtime.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Long-lived multi-agent sessions need a product **freshness contract** after a CLI or deposit upgrade. Disk can show the new generation while a running session still executes the pre-upgrade payload it loaded earlier.

## Expected

1. Generation handshake on successful upgrade/apply (monotonic token).
2. Session bind of the generation loaded into runtime context.
3. freshness verb/report: bound vs live across surface set; states current | stale_soft | stale_hard.
4. In-product soft vs hard definitions and rebind guidance without full host restart.
5. Mid-mission safety: park/hand off before hard refresh; empty session after refresh is not work complete.
6. Host-agnostic API shape (not tied to one host session-key mechanism).

## Non-goals

- Restarting the whole shared runtime as the freshness mechanism.
- Auto-resetting sessions on any file mtime change.
- Bound proof for remote PR claims (#3120).
narratives.Labels: enhancement, context-engineering, agent-experience, runtime-portability, urgent, vendored-deposit, area:cli, dogfood, enterprise-crew
narratives.UserStory: As an operator of long-lived multi-agent sessions, I want a product signal that compares the generation my session bound to the live deposit generation, so that I do not trust disk-only version probes when the agent is still running pre-upgrade payload.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Step 1: On successful deposit apply/refresh (packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts and related), stamp a monotonic generation token (file or manifest field) for the live deposit. Step 2: Add packages/core freshness module (e.g. packages/core/src/freshness/) with types for bound generation, live generation, surface set, and state enum current|stale_soft|stale_hard; unit tests for each state. Step 3: Expose CLI/task verb (deft freshness / task freshness:report or session:freshness) that reports bound vs live and differing surfaces; document rebind without full host restart and mid-mission park/handoff. Step 4: Wire session:start or session-ready optional bind/record of generation when payload surfaces load. Step 5: Product docs (content/docs or commands.md) for soft vs hard meanings. Step 6: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] for #3117. Verification: vitest on freshness module; CLI smoke; task verify:forward-coverage.
